a. At $\alpha=0.05$, test $H_0:\mu=6$ against $H_a:\mu<6$.

b. Find the median and compare it with the mean.

c.

$$\bar{x}\pm s=[2.985,7.935],$$

records.clean_question:
A random sample of six client-entertainment expenses, in dollars, is

$$157,132,109,145,125,139.$$

a. Calculate $\bar{x}$, $s^2$, and $s$. Verify $s^2$ using both the deviation formula and the computational formula.

b. Assuming an approximately normal distribution, estimate the intervals containing $68.26\%$, $95.44\%$, and $99.73\%$ of expenses.

c. Is an expense of $190$ unusually high?

d. Compute the z-score of each sampled expense.
records.clean_answer:
a. The sum is 807, so

$$\bar{x}=807/6=134.5.$$

The sum of squared deviations is $1383.5$, hence

$$s^2=\frac{1383.5}{5}=276.7,\qquad s=\sqrt{276.7}\approx16.634.$$

The computational formula gives the same result:

$$s^2=\frac{\sum x_i^2-(\sum x_i)^2/n}{n-1}=\frac{109925-807^2/6}{5}=276.7.$$

b. The estimated intervals are

$$\bar{x}\pm s=[117.866,151.134],$$

$$\bar{x}\pm2s=[101.232,167.768],$$

$$\bar{x}\pm3s=[84.598,184.402].$$

c. Yes. Since $190>184.402$, it lies more than three sample standard deviations above the mean and is unusually high under the normal model.

d. In the data order, the z-scores are approximately

$$1.353,-0.150,-1.533,0.631,-0.571,0.271.$$

a. Calculate the mean and sample standard deviation.

records.clean_answer:
a. The mean is $\bar{x}=36$ days and the sample standard deviation is $s\approx5.0166$ days.

b. The two-standard-deviation interval is

$$36\pm2(5.0166)=[25.967,46.033].$$

All 13 observations lie in this interval, so the observed percentage is $100\%$. For an approximately normal population, the Empirical Rule predicts about $95.44\%$; the difference is plausible for a sample of only 13 observations.

c. A 60-day time has

$$z=\frac{60-36}{5.0166}\approx4.78.$$

It is therefore extremely unusual under the approximate normal model, although not logically impossible.

records.clean_question: Fidelity Leveraged Company Stock has mean return $17.98\%$ and standard deviation $10.02\%$. Baron Opportunity Retail Stock has mean return $16.43\%$ and standard deviation $12.23\%$. Compare their relative risk using the coefficient of variation. If an investor prefers lower relative risk, which stock should the investor choose?
records.clean_answer:
The coefficient of variation is $CV=(s/\bar{x})\times100\%$. Thus,

$$CV_{\text{Fidelity}}=\frac{10.02}{17.98}\times100\%\approx55.73\%,$$

$$CV_{\text{Baron}}=\frac{12.23}{16.43}\times100\%\approx74.44\%.$$

Baron has greater variability relative to its mean return and is therefore riskier by this measure. An investor whose stated objective is lower relative risk should choose Fidelity. This comparison alone does not determine the best choice for every investor because preferences and other risk measures may differ.
